source.text: Large cell neuroendocrine NSCLC (defined as pathology with \>10% neuroendocrine components)
Unresectable, incurable and/or metastatic histologically and/or cytologically confirmed cutaneous, acral, or unknown primary melanoma (Stage IIIC or Stage IV)
Histologically and/or cytologically confirmed primary diagnosis of NSCLC which has progressed on at least 1 line and no more than 4 lines of prior therapy in the advanced/metastatic setting
Locally advanced recurrent and/or metastatic histologically and/or cytologically confirmed HNSCC
Advanced, metastatic histologically and/or cytologically confirmed colorectal adenocarcinoma
Locally advanced, recurrent, or metastatic histologically and/or cytologically confirmed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)

Recurrent, metastatic, or persistent histologically and/or cytologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), adenosquamous carcinoma, or adenocarcinoma of the cervix that is not amenable to curative treatment with surgery and/or radiation therapy
At least one measurable lesion per RECIST v1.1 (Eisenhauer 2009) following tumor resection for KSQ-004EX manufacturing
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0 or 1
Symptomatic and/or untreated brain metastases (of any size or number) including active leptomeningeal or parenchymal metastases.
Symptomatic and/or untreated brain metastases (of any size or number) including active leptomeningeal or parenchymal metastases.

Active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (including inflammatory bowel disease \[eg, Grade ≥ 2 colitis or Crohn's disease\], systemic lupus erythematosus, sarcoidosis syndrome, or Wegener syndrome \[granulomatosis with polyangiitis\], rheumatoid arthritis, etc.\]).
Seropositive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) 1 or 2 or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
active infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) or hepatitis C virus (HCV)
History of stroke, transient ischemic attack, unstable angina, or myocardial infarction, within 3 months prior to first dose of study treatment
Previous solid organ or hematopoietic cell transplant
Women who are pregnant or nursing
Need for treatment with steroids at stable doses (\> 10 mg/day prednisone or equivalent)

Known additional malignancy that is active and/or progressive requiring treatment; exceptions including basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, or other cancer for which the participants has been disease-free for at least 2 years
Suspected pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease (confirmed by radiography or computed tomography \[CT\])
